page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 16 physical CPU cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs. The CPU features 35 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for instruction set extensions like AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance contains no local SSD storage and no discrete GPUs, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a contrast between single-threaded execution and multi-core scaling. In single-core tests such as stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression, results fall into the lower percentile tier due to moderate base clock frequencies. However, multi-core benchmarks show consistent scaling across parallel tasks. Benchmarks including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core score (10,181), and PassMark CPU score (27,240.11) fall squarely in average categories. Memory throughput tests demonstrate 109.69 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 47.96 GB/sec for uncached writes. Application testing highlights steady output with 26.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance delivers predictable multi-core compute density without the premium cost associated with memory-heavy or GPU-accelerated tiers. The omission of local disk storage mandates external block storage, trading zero-latency local disk access for persistent storage decoupling. The ecs.c6.8xlarge is best suited for compute-heavy workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, CI/CD build environments, static web serving, parallel data processing, and distributed application nodes.
